name: Dick Cheney
role: US Vice President (2001-2009), Defense Secretary (1989-1993), Wyoming congressman (1979-1989)
summary: Cheney was a hawkish, conservative Republican who favoured tax cuts, a strong military, expanded presidential power and domestic oil, gas and coal development. He drove the Iraq war and the post-9/11 detention, interrogation and surveillance programs, which he defended to the end. He was pro-life and anti-gun-control, but said marriage law should be left to the states and supported same-sex unions; late in life he broke with Trump and endorsed Kamala Harris in 2024.

sources.usedFor: His House votes on aid to Nicaragua's contras (1985), the balanced-budget constitutional amendment (1982) and budgets.

abortion-legal.rationale: In 2000 he said he and Bush were 'clearly both pro-life'; in the House he opposed abortion and federal funding even in cases of rape or incest.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: In April 1985 he voted for H.J.Res. 239 approving funds for military or paramilitary operations in Nicaragua, and in June 1985 for the amendment adding $27 million in aid for the Nicaraguan democratic resistance, while voting against bills limiting force and funds in Nicaragua in 1984.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He cited budget deficits for his 1980s votes against new programs and favoured a balanced-budget amendment; in office he backed tax cuts alongside deficit reduction pledges, so the record is mixed.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He described market reforms as historical progress that raised incomes and reduced poverty.

central-planning.rationale: He blamed statism for economic stagnation and defended market-based reforms instead.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His 2024 statement condemned efforts to retain power after voters rejected a president.

decide-locally.rationale: He pressed for local control of schools (2000) and for leaving marriage law to the states, but also supported national testing under No Child Left Behind and strong federal executive power.

defeat-communism.rationale: He backed Reagan, voted for nearly all weapons systems and aid to the contras in the 1980s, and later described weapons systems as crucial to winning the Cold War.

democracy-best.rationale: He called elected democracies the only guarantee against terror and a task of his generation (2004); he did not address voters choosing badly.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He rejected Kyoto’s approach and favoured research and efficiency rather than economy-damaging mandates.

elective-rulers.rationale: He defended the voters’ decision as binding on presidential succession.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He said terrorism requires 'extraordinary measures' and defended detention and harsh interrogation as legal under presidential war powers; he did not state a general view on suspending legal protections.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He ridiculed Kerry's 'global test' and UN-approval requirement for using force (2004) and said inspections gave false comfort (2002), but also said Iran sanctions should go through the UN Security Council.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He defended allied military cooperation and later criticised Trump’s wavering commitment to NATO.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He cited Martin Luther King's 'content of their character' standard and said freedom means freedom for everybody (2000).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He promoted Wyoming oil and coal in Congress and in 2000 called for developing domestic energy supplies including drilling in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He urged renewed nuclear power development as clean, reliable electricity generation.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: On 1 October 1982 he voted for H.J.Res. 350, the constitutional amendment requiring Congress to adopt a balanced budget each year except in war or by a three-fifths vote.

force-without-un.rationale: In 2004 he criticised Kerry's view that troops should not deploy preemptively without UN or 'global test' approval, and defended the Iraq invasion as exactly right.

free-trade.rationale: He said all nations gain from wider trade and advocated hemispheric trade liberalisation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In 2000 he proposed letting younger workers invest part (2%) of their payroll tax in personal retirement accounts; this was a partial rather than complete replacement.

limit-growth.rationale: In 2000 he said the US must not accept a false choice between energy development and the environment and warned that lacking energy supply could shut down the economy.

limit-guns.rationale: In 1986 he voted for the amendment permitting interstate sales of rifles and shotguns and lessening record-keeping for firearms transactions (the McClure-Volkmer rewrite) and in 1988 against the Terrorist Firearms Detection Act (the 413-4 vote), and as vice president he signed the amicus brief backing the challengers in D.C. v. Heller.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He contrasted failing state-directed economies with successful markets and defended private allocation over government spending decisions.

military-superiority.rationale: He argued in 2000 that the US must rebuild its military so adversaries are deterred and 'fear us', and co-wrote a book arguing the world needs a powerful America.

national-mission.rationale: In 2004 he said that after removing hostile regimes, the US must 'stand up democracies' in their place and called this the task of his generation.

no-bailouts.rationale: He defended the 2008 emergency loans to automakers as 'not an unreasonable position' to avoid presiding over the industry's collapse.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In 2000 he said racial progress was real but the country still had a long way to go, citing profiling, education and income gaps; he did not address the specific claim.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He advocated minimising regulatory burdens so firms could expand and create jobs.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He promised America would remain 'the most generous provider of aid, especially for the poorest nations' and backed a 50 percent aid increase, while stressing aid is small beside trade and must be conditional.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2000, 2004 and again in 2009 he said people should be free to enter any union and that marriage is a state matter; Wikipedia reports he came to publicly support same-sex marriage after leaving office. He did not push for a federal rule.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: In 2009 he rejected moves to treat Bush-era detainee and interrogation policy as 'punishable offenses' and defended the policies as legal.

separate-church-state.rationale: He affirmed the principle of separation of church and state but rejected taking it 'to the extreme' of removing public prayer and acknowledgement of God.

separated-powers.rationale: He claimed broad presidential powers beyond statutory restriction, yet expressly accepted binding Supreme Court judgments.

simple-living.rationale: He rejected government-induced energy austerity and sought efficiency without reducing living standards.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He defended presidents overriding statutory limits in their constitutional domain but insisted on compliance with Supreme Court rulings.

strong-leader.rationale: He worked to expand presidential power and championed the unitary executive view; he also repeatedly stressed working across the aisle, so the evidence on bypassing gridlock is mixed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He supported the NSA warrantless surveillance program and defended the Patriot Act in the 2004 debate; in 2001 he said intelligence agencies should be able to use 'any means at our disposal'.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He condemned protectionism as a cause of stagnation and sought removal of import duties.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He called inheritance taxation wrong and demanded permanent repeal rather than temporary phaseout.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In the 2004 debate he argued against raising the top income tax bracket, saying it would hit small businesses, and said he and Bush would make the tax cuts permanent; in 2000 he backed across-the-board tax relief.

traditional-family.rationale: He described families as society’s building blocks while defending tax treatment supporting marriage.

notes:
Views changed on Head Start, the Education Department and the Martin Luther King holiday (he later reversed or said he would no longer oppose). His memoir In My Time (2011), Exceptional (2015) and the May 2009 AEI speech full text could not be fetched; the interrogation position rests on quoted excerpts. No answer was found for torture-specific, Iraq-WMD-specific or Trump-specific statements because none of the 490 statements addresses them directly.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 21 answers taken from it, 14 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass, all 490 statements checked, no inferred answers. No statement-specific evidence for nine of the ten priorities. His own defence of interrogations is recorded under surveillance, accountability and executive authority where wording matches; no torture-specific statement exists. Accountability and constitutional limits remain mixed because he praised punishment of Abu Ghraib abuses and accepted binding court rulings while opposing CIA accountability and statutory constraints on presidential powers. Military interventions are not automatically political violence outside lawful authority. Rejection of apartheid sanctions is not treated as approval of racial segregation. Joint town halls distinguish his words from his wife’s: her religion/history and voucher answers are not attributed to him. The 2005 pension plan only partially replaced public provision, so its answer is qualified. His personal medical technology is not a policy on human enhancement. Full 2009 AEI speech, 2015 AEI transcript, 2014 Kristol interview and other full texts downloaded. Main lane decides legacy-list changes. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by evidence; his Voteview record (House 1979-89) is cited for contra aid and the balanced-budget amendment, replacing two answers that rested on OnTheIssues; public-access-to-information, which rested only on Wikipedia, is nulled.
